clips.title: Claude Code NEW Super Review FEATURE: Anthropic just fixed SLOP CODE!?
clips.why: Anthropic's own multi-agent code review, the pattern our panel copies: several reviewers, a verification step, and severity tags.
look: Several agents look at the PR in parallel, each with its own focus: our lenses.
A verification step checks findings before they are posted: our skeptic.
Every comment gets a severity, so the important ones stand out.
clips.after: Byte's panel is the same shape, with two additions of ours: three blind lenses, and a skeptic whose cite is checked by code.

clips.title: The Death of the Code Review: What the Data Actually Says — Laurie Voss, Arize AI
clips.why: What the big automated reviewers do today, from a talk that looks at the data on AI code review.
look: How GitHub Copilot and Cursor review PRs today.
Ask yourself why a reviewer that stays silent when it has nothing important to say could be a feature.
Ask yourself which helps more: checking each finding, or adding more reviewers.
clips.after: On Nova's PRs, Byte posts only new high and medium findings, because Nova will act on every single one.

clips.title: An Invisible Comment Hijacks Your AI Code Reviewer (Azure DevOps)
clips.why: A real proof of concept: a hidden comment in a PR description gives an AI reviewer new orders.
look: The instructions hide in an HTML comment that people cannot see.
The agent reads the PR and its goal changes.
Nothing in the code was wrong; the attack was in the text around it.
clips.after: That is why Nova's receipt is data: it can mark a finding known, but only the code at head can show it is fixed.

clips.title: The Death of the Code Review: What the Data Actually Says — Laurie Voss, Arize AI
clips.why: Who reviews the reviewers: prompt injection against AI review, from the same talk.
look: An AI reviewer reads untrusted text in every PR.
What an attacker gains by steering the reviewer.
Ask yourself where the defence should sit: inside the model, or outside it?
clips.after: Our defences sit outside the model: playbooks baked into the image, blind lenses with no gh, and code that checks every skeptic cite.

practice.q: A person opens a draft PR in fcp. Does Byte review it?

options.text: Yes, every PR is reviewed when it is opened
options.why: fcp's workflow lets opened through only for the agents' App, so human drafts are not reviewed at open.

options.text: No, drafts are reviewed only when the author is rhino-ai-agents[bot] with a valid Requested-by line
options.why: That narrow exception exists because Nova waits in draft for Byte.

options.text: Yes, but only the sniff runs
options.why: The sniff only runs on pushes after a first review. A human draft gets no review yet.

practice.q: Complete the line Byte's gate looks for in Nova's PR body.
practice.hint: The same line the independent-approval check reads.
practice.why: It names the person who handed Nova the ticket; Byte checks that this person has write access today.

practice.q: A medium finding has the category naming, and naming is quiet for the frontend team. On Nova's frontend PR, what happens to it?

options.why: Quiet categories are counted, not posted, on agent PRs.

options.text: It is counted in the quiet row of the severity table
options.why: Nothing disappears: it shows as a number in the check run.

options.text: It is deleted from the run
options.why: Counted findings stay visible as numbers; they are just not comments.

practice.q: Put the panel's steps in order.
items: The runner fetches the diff once into a file
Five lenses review in parallel, three of them blind
The skeptic answers confirmed, refuted or unsure with a file:line cite
Code checks each cite, drops refuted findings and lowers unsure ones
Survivors are ranked, capped at 25 and posted through the usual path
practice.why: Cheap code steps (dedupe, cite check) sit around the expensive model steps, so the skeptic sees fewer findings and its answers are checked.

practice.q: Which lens reads the PR title and body?

options.why: Correctness is blind: diff and code only.
It compares the change with what was asked, so it needs the title, the body and, later, the ticket.
Security is blind too, so text in the PR cannot steer it.
